Maria: rolling adaptive continuous-batcher v2 to canary now (03:10 UTC). minor config tilt: token_budget_target=256, merge_timer=off for short queues. will watch p95 and kernel selection churn

perf-bot: deployment v2 applied to canary pool gpu-cluster-7 (canary=10%). monitoring: latency, kernel-switches, kv-hit-rate

Kunal: noticed any kernel affinity changes in the rollout? last time affinity flips caused p95 spikes for small-reqs

Sam: yes, v2 adds a shape-priority heuristic that prefers small-batch low-latency kernels but only if batch_size>=4. with merge_timer disabled we see more 1-2 sized batches, so runtime ends up switching kernels more often

Irene: quick snapshot from canary over last 8m:
```
pre-rollout: p95=230ms, avg_batch=5.9, kv_hit=0.72, kernel_switches=1400
post-rollout: p95=520ms, avg_batch=3.1, kv_hit=0.41, kernel_switches=3620
throughput: -12% vs baseline
errors: no increase in errors, but tail latency up
```

Lee: that KV hit drop is suspicious. are we invalidating prefixes when the batching window changes?

Sam: probable. v2's aggressive prefix aggregation defers prefix caching until batch forms; with smaller batches we miss the cache warm-up window. so more KV cache misses -> longer slow-path latency -> different kernels used (slow-path kernels)

Kunal: can you grep the runtime logs for `kernel_select` events around the long tails? want to see if selection_reason=shape or selection_reason=kv_miss

Sam: done, snippets: `2026-02-15T03:12:21Z kernel_select: reason=kv_miss kernel=slow_path_v3` repeated for many small requests. also `batch_form: size=1 timer=0ms`

Maria: oof. merge_timer=off was to reduce join latency for high-throughput flows but it's hurting small-chat workloads. suggestion: re-enable merge_timer but adjust token_budget_target down slightly to preserve cost benefits

Irene: quick A/B from canary slices: re-enable merge_timer -> p95 drops to ~240ms, avg_batch=5.6, kv_hit=0.69, kernel_switches=1500; still slightly better token utilization vs pre-v1 because token_budget_target kept at 384 instead of 512

Lee: so root cause = interaction between merge_timer disable + shape-priority heuristic + lower token_budget_target leading to batch shapes that trigger kernel fallback and KV warmup regression

Kunal: good postmortem hypothesis. action items?

Maria: 1) rollback merge_timer toggle for canary (doing now). 2) create perf experiment matrix: token_budget_target in [384, 448, 512], merge_timer on/off, measure p95/kv_hit/kernel_switches. 3) add an instrumentation flag `selection_reason` to traces so we can aggregate reasons for kernel_select at scale.

Sam: I'll push a hotfix to re-enable merge_timer on canary, and start the experiment harness against a 20% slice. ETA 30m

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: re-enable merge_timer on gpu-cluster-7 canary slice. change set by Sam.

Irene: after re-enable we already see p95 ~260ms in first 5m. keep watching for regressions during peak traffic

Maria: thanks. let's not ship v2-wide until experiment matrix completes and we add the `selection_reason` metric. putting a block on rollout until follow-ups done :no_entry_sign:

Lee: noted. will draft a short docs blurb about heuristics interactions and add to the rollout checklist (merge_timer toggles, kv-warm windows)

Kunal: thanks team. ping me if the experiment shows any odd kernel affinity thrashing, will instrument deeper profiler on the affected nodes

Maria: ack, thanks :thumbsup:
